context: Operator confirmed 2026-10-24, answer verbatim: "Confirmo, corrigir na rc-2 (Recomendado)". Found by the rc-2 Job 3 review (verdict 2026-10-24T184749Z, MEDIUM). repro: PYTHONPATH=repos/rand-engine uv run --no-project --with numpy python -c "import numpy as np; print(sum(all(np.random.default_rng(s).integers(-86400, 86400, 10) >= 0) for s in range(100000)))" (prints about 98: the all-non-negative rate of 10 draws over that range, the test's failure rate)

title: Spark pre-1970 test asserts a negative epoch on 10 unseeded rows, so it fails at random

cause: FileHandler.handle_path returned an empty dirname for a bare name, so the stream writer joined it into an absolute root path; the batch writer patched the same case with its own fallback (two deciders)
context: Standing operator confirmation (every found bug: register and fix, never ask); found by the main thread's 0.8.2 grill probes, 2026-10-30, on the work branch at 3fcd389 (published as 0.8.1). Block-list item (5): data loss outside the requested path. Contract: FileStreamWriter.start(path) writes the stream under path (its docstring example writes under a temporary directory). Present since 828cd86.
expected: A bare name resolves relative to the current directory (start('tmp') writes under ./tmp), and overwrite removes only files this stream wrote under that path, never entries of another directory.
repro: PYTHONPATH=repos/rand-engine uv run -q --no-project --with numpy --with pandas --with pyarrow python -c "from rand_engine import DataGenerator; from rand_engine.file_handlers.file_handler import FileHandler; b, f, _ = FileHandler.handle_path('tmp', 'csv', {}); print('start(tmp) targets', f'{b}/{f}'); DataGenerator({'a': {'method': 'integers', 'kwargs': {'min': 0, 'max': 9}}}, seed=1).size(5).writeStream.format('csv').mode('overwrite').option('timeout', 0.05).start('ages')" (prints 'start(tmp) targets /tmp', then raises PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/ages'; no file is touched)
solution: handle_path returns '.' for an empty dirname, the one decider; the batch writer's duplicate fallback is deleted
symptom: start(path) joins f'{base_path}/{name}' (line 100) where base_path is os.path.dirname(path), empty for a bare name, so start('tmp') targets /tmp and start('ages') targets /ages. With mode('overwrite') the loop at lines 108-111 then calls os.remove on every entry of that directory: a safe run with os.remove replaced by a recorder passed every pre-existing entry of /tmp to it, and start('data') in a container would target /data.
title: writeStream.start with a bare name writes under the filesystem root, and overwrite deletes that root directory's files

Contract: specs/constitution.md invariant 3, 'A spec that validates generates'. Structural cause: the validator re-implements each gen_* precondition by hand (validators 1,260 lines against a NumPy core of 535), so it trails the engine; the archived ledger holds this class repeatedly, each closed by one more rule. expected: Every spec that DataGenerator accepts generates: each of the six is refused at construction with a SpecValidationError naming the column, the parameter and the fix, from one source of the method rules rather than a hand-kept copy.

title: Six spec shapes pass DataGenerator validation, then fail in generation with a raw engine error

context: Standing operator confirmation (every found bug: register and fix, never ask); found by the main thread's 0.8.2 grill probes, 2026-10-30, on 3fcd389 (published 0.8.1). Contract: a distincts_prop weight is a value's relative frequency; the validator checks only that each weight is an integer, and gen_distincts_prop builds its pool with range(weight), so a negative weight yields no entries instead of a refusal.
expected: A negative weight is refused at construction with a SpecValidationError naming the column and the value; every accepted value can appear in the output.
repro: PYTHONPATH=repos/rand-engine uv run -q --no-project --with numpy --with pandas --with pyarrow python -c "from rand_engine import DataGenerator; df = DataGenerator({'c': {'method': 'distincts_prop', 'kwargs': {'distincts': {'a': -1, 'b': 2}}}}, seed=1).size(1000).get_df(); print('distincts_prop {a: -1, b: 2} validated; value counts:', df['c'].value_counts().to_dict())" (exit 0; prints value counts: {'b': 1000})

title: distincts_prop accepts a negative weight and silently drops that value from the output

context: Standing operator confirmation (every found bug: register and fix, never ask); found by the main thread's 0.8.2 grill probes, 2026-10-30, on 3fcd389 (published 0.8.1). Contract: a RandSpec maps each output column to one definition; no validator checks output names across columns, and generate_first_level assigns each cols name into one dict, so the later definition replaces the earlier column.
expected: A spec whose output column names collide (a key, or a name in cols, used twice) is refused at construction with a SpecValidationError naming the duplicated column and both definitions.
repro: PYTHONPATH=repos/rand-engine uv run -q --no-project --with numpy --with pandas --with pyarrow python -c "from rand_engine import DataGenerator; spec = {'a': {'method': 'integers', 'kwargs': {'min': 0, 'max': 9}}, 'm': {'method': 'distincts_map', 'cols': ['a', 'b'], 'kwargs': {'distincts': {'x': ['y']}}}}; df = DataGenerator(spec, seed=1).size(5).get_df(); print('validated; columns:', list(df.columns), '| a:', df['a'].tolist())" (exit 0; prints columns: ['a', 'b'] | a: ['x', 'x', 'x', 'x', 'x'])
symptom: Spec {'a': integers 0..9, 'm': distincts_map with cols ['a', 'b']} validates; the frame has columns ['a', 'b'] and 'a' holds the map keys ('x') instead of the integers, which vanish without an error or warning.
title: A correlated column whose cols names an existing column validates and silently overwrites it

context: Standing operator confirmation (every found bug: register and fix, never ask); found by dd-code-reviewer on the hotfix of writestream-bare-name-targets-filesystem-root (verdict 2026-10-31T023517Z), on the work branch at ac30edb. Severity CRITICAL: data loss (dd-bug-registration severity scale; block-list item 5), off the default path: it needs Windows and a drive-relative path. Contract: rand_engine/file_handlers/_writer_stream.py:68-72, FileStreamWriter.start(path) writes the stream under path. Evidence is the path resolution under ntpath; not run on a Windows host.
expected: A drive-relative path resolves the way a path join does ('C:ages' stays under drive C's current directory), as the batch writer already resolves it; overwrite never clears a directory outside the requested path.
repro: PYTHONPATH=repos/rand-engine uv run -q --no-project --with numpy --with pandas --with pyarrow python -c "import ntpath, types; import rand_engine.file_handlers.file_handler as fh; fh.os = types.SimpleNamespace(path=ntpath); b, f, _ = fh.FileHandler.handle_path('C:ages', 'csv', {}); s = f'{b}/{f}'; print('start(C:ages) targets', s, '| isabs:', ntpath.isabs(s), '| path join gives', ntpath.join(b, f), '| isabs:', ntpath.isabs(ntpath.join(b, f)))" (prints 'start(C:ages) targets C:/ages | isabs: True | path join gives C:ages | isabs: False', exit 0; nothing is written or deleted)
symptom: start(path) builds the target as the string f'{base_path}/{name}' (line 100). For 'C:ages', ntpath.dirname gives 'C:', which handle_path keeps, and the string join yields 'C:/ages': the ages directory at the root of drive C, not under drive C's current directory. With mode('overwrite') the loop at lines 108-111 then calls os.remove on every entry of that directory. The batch writer joins with pathlib and keeps 'C:ages' drive-relative.
title: writeStream.start with a Windows drive-relative path ('C:ages') writes under the drive root, and overwrite clears that directory
